resources.string: Turn a compatible Android phone into a wireless PowerPoint remote. No mobile data, internet connection or Windows companion app required.
Connect your Windows laptop to the projector, open PowerPoint and turn on Bluetooth.
Turn on Bluetooth on your phone. Use SlidePilot pairing controls or your system Bluetooth settings to pair the phone and laptop.
In SlidePilot, choose the paired laptop and tap Connect. Wait for the Connected status before sending commands.
Start the slideshow on the laptop or in SlidePilot. Tap Next and Previous to navigate from anywhere within Bluetooth range.
Starts the slideshow from the beginning (F5).
Starts from the current slide (Shift + F5).
Track your speaking time with Start, Pause and Reset. Starting the slideshow from SlidePilot can start the timer automatically.
When enabled, the physical volume buttons can navigate slides while SlidePilot has focus and a valid connection.
Review connection state changes and background Bluetooth operations. Copy or clear the log when troubleshooting.
The quick-help instructions from your existing SlidePilot app are preserved below.
Paired does not mean connected. Wait for SlidePilot to report Connected.
If a connection fails, check Bluetooth on both devices, reconnect or remove and pair the devices again.
The Bluetooth HID feature depends on phone firmware. Android version alone does not guarantee compatibility.
Slide commands act on the focused laptop application. Keep the PowerPoint slideshow active.
Designed for presentations, classroom talks and meetings. SlidePilot sends keyboard-style commands directly over Bluetooth to compatible computers. Presentation files stay on your laptop.
Note: Opening this guide can pause the current Bluetooth session. If disconnected, reconnect when you return to the remote.
